original_question: Do the two equivalence relations on ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed links - homeomorphism and virtual equivalence via generalized Kirby moves - actually coincide? More generally, give a geometric-topological interpretation of virtual 3-manifolds, and determine whether the alternative construction obtained by doing surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R up to stabilization yields the same theory.
correct_elements: Your draft captures all three components of the paper's actual problem very closely: (i) whether, for ordinary 3-manifolds given by surgery on framed links, virtual Kirby equivalence collapses to the usual classical/homeomorphism equivalence; (ii) the request for a geometric-topological interpretation of a virtual 3-manifold; and (iii) the comparison with an alternative construction via surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g × R up to stabilization.
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem in Section 8.1, item 5, not as a theorem or conjecture elsewhere.

'Virtual 3-manifolds' are introduced here as formal equivalence classes of virtual diagrams modulo generalized Kirby moves; because the question is about surgery presentations, the intended objects are framed virtual link diagrams.

The classical comparison is quantified as follows: given two ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed links K and L, assume K and L are equivalent through the virtual Kirby calculus; does it follow that K and L are equivalent through the classical Kirby calculus?

The nearby topological context for 'S_g × R up to stabilization' comes from Section 2.3: stabilization means isotopy in the thickened surfaces, homeomorphisms of the surfaces, and addition or subtraction of empty handles.
The alternative construction is not meant abstractly; it is to be compared specifically with the virtual-3-manifold theory referenced there as that of Kauffman and Dye [40].
No ambient ring, field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier conditions occur in this problem.
refined_question: Let a virtual 3-manifold mean a formal equivalence class of framed virtual link diagrams modulo the generalized Kirby moves of Kauffman and Dye. For ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed classical links K and L, does equivalence of K and L in the virtual Kirby calculus imply equivalence in the classical Kirby calculus (hence no new equivalence beyond the usual one for ordinary 3-manifolds)? More generally, can one give a geometric-topological interpretation of these virtual 3-manifold classes, and does the alternative construction obtained by performing surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g × R modulo stabilization—i.e. isotopy in the thickened surfaces, homeomorphism of the surface, and addition/removal of empty handles—coincide with the Kauffman-Dye theory?
justification: The draft is aimed squarely at the paper's Section 8.1, Problem 5, whose wording matches it almost verbatim. I therefore kept the scope exactly at that item rather than broadening to neighboring questions about virtual invariants or Kirby-type constructions. I used Section 2.3 and Theorem 2.1 only to unpack the paper's intended meaning of 'links in thickened surfaces S_g × R considered up to stabilization,' which is the only substantial hidden definition needed to make the question stand alone. The paper does not prove an equivalence between the two proposed virtual-3-manifold constructions, so there is no paper-certified alternate formulation to supply.
